notes.text: Aleksander Barkov is day to day (knee injury) and has missed the last 21 games. He is one of their best players.
Brad Marchand is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-six forward.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Justin Holl has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jack St. Ivany has taken his spot beside Cole Hutson. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 111:20 together.

Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve (knee surgery) and has missed the last 16 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 121:13 together.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 8% last season.

stakes: The Panthers go in fifth in the Atlantic with 27 points, the Capitals sixth in the Metropolitan with 20 points.

story.head: The Capitals are searching for answers
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in Washington on Nov 7. The Capitals are on a four-game losing streak, and the Panthers (12-8-3) lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Nov 17. Going in, the Panthers are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Capitals sixth in the Metropolitan (25th).

The Panthers’ record (.587) is about what their chances are worth. The Capitals have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .568, and their goaltending has held them back.
This season, the Capitals have been outscored 76-67, even though they’ve outscored teams 50-48 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 17-12.

The Panthers are the league’s most physical team: first in forecheck pressure, first in physicality and first in rough stuff. On the other side, the Capitals get the league’s best looks (1st) and get their shots through to the net (5th). They also have a leaky penalty kill (27th), so the Panthers’ power play (3rd) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Washington has allowed 3.80 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. That means the Capitals wait for good looks, but the Cats settle for hopeful ones.

Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 25 A / 32 P in 23 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL. Sam Reinhart (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, with six goals in ten games against Washington since 2023-24. Alex Tuch (13 G / 3 A / 16 P in 20 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead, with a point in six straight games against Florida. Ryan Leonard (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 20 GP) shares it.
Jacob Markström (6-4-1 / .897 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Florida, and Logan Thompson (7-6-0 / .879 SV% in 15 GS) for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Tuch out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Verhaeghe, Reinhart and Eller.
